sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Scientific Agent Skills is a collection of 177 research skills for AI agents from K-Dense. They teach agents like Claude Code, Codex and Cursor how to use scientific libraries, databases and workflows across biology, chemistry, medicine, physics, engineering and data analysis.
sixtySeconds.problem: General-purpose agents can call any Python package, but they often don't know the right tools or steps for specialised science. These skills give them curated guidance for tasks like single-cell RNA-seq, molecular docking or astronomical data analysis.
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for broad, curated coverage of scientific domains, following the open Agent Skills standard so it works with many agent hosts. It was formerly called Claude Scientific Skills.
requirements: An Agent Skills host such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or Gemini CLI
Node.js for npx, or GitHub CLI 2.90+

overview: Domains include bioinformatics and genomics, cheminformatics and drug discovery, proteomics, clinical research, medical imaging, neuroscience, machine learning, materials science, physics and astronomy, engineering, geospatial science, lab automation, scientific communication and research methodology.

Install with npx skills, a standards-based installer for supported hosts, or with gh skill from the GitHub CLI, which can install one skill or target a specific agent. The collection is also an Agent Plugins package.

Health-related skills are framed for research only, not patient diagnosis or treatment decisions. The project is described in an arXiv paper and is MIT licensed. K-Dense also offers K-Dense BYOK, a free desktop co-scientist built on these skills.
limitations: Research use only for clinical and health skills
Results depend on your agent and model
Some skills need specialised Python packages
